q: How do rejected batches and yield losses affect our product carbon footprint?
title: Rejects and yield loss in a footprint
short: They raise it. Emissions from making rejects are spread over the good units you sell, because the energy was used either way. Divide total emissions by good output, not by gross production. Rejects you recycle or sell as scrap can carry a share if they have a market value.

p: Product footprint equals emissions of the process divided by sellable output. A 5 per cent reject rate lifts the footprint by a little over 5 per cent.

ul: Sold as a co-product with value: allocate by economic value or mass, and state which.
Scrapped or reworked internally: no allocation, the good units carry it.

p: Cutting rejects is often the cheapest way to lower a footprint per unit, and buyers recognise it as real.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and production documents into dated, fingerprinted plant records, so the monthly intensity behind a figure can be traced to its source.
